results.name: family_leeds_budget
results.reply:
I've switched the weights to the family preset. Within your £350k budget, **Garforth East** comes out top in Leeds. It's the best all-rounder here, with strong safety and community scores. Meanwood and Chapel Allerton North have the strongest school scores, but their safety scores are weaker.

**Guiseley** and **Yeadon** are cheaper, but they rank lower overall. Churwell's place in the list is unstable, so treat it with caution. The prices are area medians, not family-house prices.

I can look at schools near any of these if that would help.

results.name: commuter_manchester
results.reply: I've set the weights to the commuter preset. With transport counting most, most of the top ten are in or right next to the city centre, like New Islington, Ancoats and Castlefield. They have excellent transport and amenities but score low on safety. Sale Central and Timperley in Trafford, on the Metrolink line, are a good balance: safer, greener and with strong schools. Timperley's typical prices are roughly double, though. Crime figures for Greater Manchester are estimates, so take the safety scores with some caution. I can narrow this down by budget or set a minimum safety score if you'd like.

results.name: retiree_devon
results.reply:
I've set up a "Quiet, Safe Retirement" profile that gives extra weight to safety and quiet. One catch: "Devon" was read as **North Devon** council only, so these rankings cover just that part of the county. **Braunton** and **Fremington & Instow** come out on top, with strong safety scores and good access to health services, which matters in retirement. **Bratton Fleming** is the safest of the lot, but it has very few shops and services nearby.

I can run the same search for East Devon, the South Hams, Teignbridge or Torridge to cover the rest of the county.

results.name: safest_bristol
results.reply: I searched within 10 km of Bristol, so most of the safest neighbourhoods are in the suburbs just outside the city council boundary: Downend North and Emersons Green in South Gloucestershire, and Backwell in North Somerset. Westbury-on-Trym is the highest-ranked area inside the City of Bristol itself, and it also scores well on schools and amenities, though its typical house prices are the highest on this list. I can narrow this to the City of Bristol council area only if you'd like.

results.name: brighton_street_level_budget
results.reply: I found 73 small areas in Brighton and Hove where the typical price is under £400k. Central Seven Dials and Goldsmid score highest overall, mainly because transport and shops and nightlife are excellent. Round Hill and St James's Street score poorly on safety. If you'd rather have somewhere calmer, Withdean Woods and Mile Oak are the safest and greenest, but there's less nearby. The under-£400k prices are likely to be mostly flats, so I can compare a few of these side by side, or re-rank them by what matters most to you.

results.name: young_professional_london
results.reply:
I've set you up with a Young Professional profile, which puts the most weight on nightlife, transport and cost. On that basis, Rotherhithe, East Village (Stratford) and Leamouth come top. They have excellent transport and plenty going on, and they're cheaper than the Clapham and Earlsfield areas in Wandsworth. Those Wandsworth areas have a stronger community feel but much higher house prices. Most of the top areas score fairly low on safety.

This search only covered areas within 10 km of central London. If you tell me your budget or roughly where your office is, I can narrow it down.

results.name: profile_postcode
results.reply:
LS6 3AA is in Headingley, Leeds. It scores better than 72% of neighbourhoods in the UK and Ireland, thanks to excellent amenities, a GP and supermarket very close by, good transport and lots of trees. The big drawback is safety: burglary, theft and road collisions are all very high, putting it in the bottom 5%. Very few households have children, which fits Headingley's large student population.

The typical house price is an estimate because it's based on few sales. The council tax figure is the Band D rate for all of Leeds, not this street. I can compare it with nearby areas like Meanwood or Roundhay if you're looking for somewhere safer.

results.name: profile_place
results.reply: I used the Whitley Bay Promenade area in the town centre. Overall it scores better than 43% of UK and Ireland neighbourhoods. Amenities and nightlife are excellent, and schools, GPs, broadband and air quality are good. The weak spots are safety (bottom 3%: high anti-social behaviour and violent crime), typical house prices of about £349k and a low score for community and wellbeing. Those weak spots are common in busy seafront centres. The quieter residential streets inland could score quite differently, so it's worth comparing a few Whitley Bay neighbourhoods.

results.name: compare_two
results.reply: I compared the Headingley neighbourhood of Leeds with Chapel Allerton North, which is the neighbourhood the tool matched for Chapel Allerton. Chapel Allerton scores a little higher overall, with better results for safety (notably burglary), schools, environment and community. Headingley is stronger on amenities, nightlife and transport, and typical house prices there are lower. I can rank nearby north Leeds areas with your priorities if that would help.

results.name: compare_three_bristol
results.reply: Clifton Village comes out on top, helped by stronger schools and community scores. Redland & St Andrew's is close behind and is the most expensive of the three. Bedminster is clearly cheaper, with transport and amenities about as good, but its safety score is much lower: its violent crime rate is roughly four times the other two. If price matters, it would be worth looking at Bedminster street by street to find the calmer pockets.

results.name: well_run_pubs

Most are to the south, around Victoria and St James's Park, and The Phoenix is closest. "Well-run" only reflects hygiene ratings, not the beer or atmosphere. Bbar is the one listed with outdoor seating.

results.name: nearest_gp
results.reply: The closest GP practices are Ancoats Urban Village Medical Practice and New Islington Medical Centre. They share a site at M4 6EE, about 770 m east of M1 1AE. City Health Centre (M1 1PL) is about the same distance to the west. These are straight-line distances, so the walk will be a bit longer. It's worth checking which practices cover your address before you try to register.

results.name: explain_safety_gmp
results.reply: I used Castlefield & Deansgate, where safety scores just 7.5. Every crime measure is near the bottom, and serious road collisions nearby are among the worst anywhere. Treat the crime figures as estimates: Greater Manchester Police publishes no street-level data, so they're worked out from the 2025 deprivation index. Rates are also counted per resident, which makes busy centres with many visitors and few residents look worse than daily life there may feel.

results.name: explain_high_score
results.reply:
I used Hampstead Town in Camden, north London. It scores 67, better than 77% of neighbourhoods across the UK and Ireland. Most of that comes from four themes that are close to the top of the scale: amenities, transport, health services and schools. Lots of tree cover, green space and a mild climate add a bit more.

Two themes pull the score down a lot. Safety is weak because burglary, theft and anti-social behaviour rates are high, and Housing is weak because typical prices are around £1.4m. If those don't worry you, I could raise the weights on the themes it does well on, or rank nearby areas that are safer.

results.name: least_noise_london
results.reply: Greenwich Peninsula East is well ahead of the rest, with very few homes exposed to transport or industrial noise. Next come leafy residential pockets like Belsize Park, Furzedown West and Graveney. Of these, Furzedown and West Norwood/Streatham also score well on environment and are cheaper. This search only covered 10 km around central London. I can widen it to outer boroughs, or rank by night-time noise instead.

The index also measures nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), which mostly comes from traffic and shows busy roads and city centres more sharply. I can switch the map to NO₂, or list the cleanest-air areas in a region you're looking at.

results.name: shortlist_add

results.reply:
The schools and childcare theme scores four things: good primary schools nearby (England only), good secondary schools nearby (England, Wales and Scotland), choice of good schools, and good nurseries nearby (both across the UK). It also shows primary and secondary exam results for England, but these don't count towards the score.

The data doesn't include any measures for Ireland. Northern Ireland only gets school choice and nursery access. I can rank areas by any of these measures if you'd like.

results.name: compare_top_two_followup
results.reply: These two are effectively tied overall but are quite different places. Garforth East, a commuter town east of Leeds, has clearly lower crime and somewhat cheaper homes. Far Headingley & Weetwood is better connected, with more amenities, closer shops and GPs and slightly greener surroundings, but has more crime. If you want somewhere quieter and safer, go for Garforth; if you want things on your doorstep, go for Headingley. I can save either one to your shortlist.

results.name: reweight_followup
results.reply:

Strensall and Bishopthorpe & Copmanthorpe come into the top eight as the safest options, though they have fewer shops and amenities and worse transport.

If you'd rather be able to walk to shops and cafés, South Bank & Dringhouses or Acomb are a good middle ground. I can also look up the GPs and pharmacies nearest any of these areas.

results.name: ambiguous_clapham

The trade-offs are the remoteness (the nearest GP is about 6.7 km away in a straight line, and there are few shops, nurseries or good rail services), high house prices for the area and a grey, wet climate, so it ranks in the bottom 11% overall across the UK and Ireland. Did you mean Clapham in south London? I can profile that one instead.

results.name: ambiguous_newport
results.reply:
I used Newport in Wales, which points to Stow Hill in the city centre. It scores better than 70% of UK and Ireland neighbourhoods. It does very well for amenities, health services, transport and schools, though the schools score comes from council-wide exam results, so treat it as an estimate. The big downside is safety: crime is among the highest in Wales. Community and wellbeing is also weak.

City centres often score like this, so a council-wide comparison would show more of Newport. Did you mean a different Newport, like the one on the Isle of Wight or in Shropshire?
